drhp.business: The Company manufactures Writing & Printing Paper and Kraft Paper. Writing & Printing Paper is made using agricultural residues such as wheat straw, bagasse, sarkanda, softwood pulp and other fillers, while Kraft Paper is made using wastepaper and agricultural residues such as bagasse, wheat straw and sarkanda. The Company has made proactive investments in chemical recovery, effluent treatment and power co-generation plants alongside the consumption of renewable agro-based raw material.

risks.note: Non-compliance with environmental regulations poses a serious threat to operational continuity; mitigated via an effluent treatment plant and a chemical recovery unit that recycles black liquor from the pulping process.

Interruptions in raw material supply could impair efficiency, cause production delays, raise costs and reduce profitability; the Company diversifies its raw material base (bagasse, wheat straw, sarkanda, recycled domestic and imported waste paper) and maintains substantial year-round bagasse inventory.

Entry of new players threatens market share and profit margins; the Company relies on its status as a premier Indian manufacturer of printing and kraft paper and cost advantages from agricultural-residue-based inputs.
Inability to attract, retain and develop skilled professionals may compromise product quality, hinder innovation and affect performance; mitigated through continuous training and development.
Failure to uphold quality standards could reduce product demand and impact sales and revenue; mitigated via a rigorous quality control process and certifications (IS 14490:2024, ISO 9001:2015).

Insufficient liquidity could restrict the Company's ability to meet financial obligations and affect long-term viability; the Company cites an inventory turnover ratio of 84 days and a debt-equity ratio of 0.23x as of FY26 as mitigants.

Additional capacity coming online across the paper industry kept supply elevated and paper prices under pressure through FY 2025-26, weighing on realisations and margins; the Writing & Printing Paper segment specifically saw NSR decline.

The Company's promoter and erstwhile Managing Director, Umesh Chander Garg, passed away on 23 January 2026, leaving the Managing Director position vacant until Jatinder Singh was appointed on 9 April 2026.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- technology: WPP machine speed upgrade from 640 mpm to 800 mpm (800-900 mpm per highlights) via a Bellmer shoe press — evidence: modernisation capex of ~₹125 Crore materially expanding throughput capacity
- cost position: uses agricultural residues (bagasse, wheat straw, sarkanda) as raw material — evidence: company states this effectively lowers raw material costs and enhances cost competitiveness versus new entrants
- customer lock-in: decades-long partnerships with institutional buyers, traders and channel partners — evidence: described as the backbone of the Company's marketing success

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Non-compliance with environmental regulations poses a serious threat to operational continuity; mitigated via an effluent treatment plant and a chemical recovery unit that recycles black liquor from the pulping process.
- Interruptions in raw material supply could impair efficiency, cause production delays, raise costs and reduce profitability; the Company diversifies its raw material base (bagasse, wheat straw, sarkanda, recycled domestic and imported waste paper) and maintains substantial year-round bagasse inventory.
- Entry of new players threatens market share and profit margins; the Company relies on its status as a premier Indian manufacturer of printing and kraft paper and cost advantages from agricultural-residue-based inputs.
- Inability to attract, retain and develop skilled professionals may compromise product quality, hinder innovation and affect performance; mitigated through continuous training and development.
- Failure to uphold quality standards could reduce product demand and impact sales and revenue; mitigated via a rigorous quality control process and certifications (IS 14490:2024, ISO 9001:2015).
- Insufficient liquidity could restrict the Company's ability to meet financial obligations and affect long-term viability; the Company cites an inventory turnover ratio of 84 days and a debt-equity ratio of 0.23x as of FY26 as mitigants.
- Additional capacity coming online across the paper industry kept supply elevated and paper prices under pressure through FY 2025-26, weighing on realisations and margins; the Writing & Printing Paper segment specifically saw NSR decline.
- The Company's promoter and erstwhile Managing Director, Umesh Chander Garg, passed away on 23 January 2026, leaving the Managing Director position vacant until Jatinder Singh was appointed on 9 April 2026.
